chapters.title: 2 Timothy 1 — Guarding the gospel and rekindling the gift
chapters.historicalContext: Paul writes to Timothy near the end of his life, aware of suffering and the possibility of death. He encourages Timothy to remain courageous and faithful to the gospel entrusted to him.
chapters.overview: Paul remembers Timothy's sincere faith, urges him to rekindle God's gift, and calls him not to be ashamed of the testimony about Christ or of Paul's imprisonment. The gospel is the foundation of hope and faithful endurance.
chapters.studyObservation: The Spirit gives power, love, and self-control rather than fear. Paul's appeal is both personal and doctrinal: guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit.
chapters.connectionNotes: Read with chapter 2's call to endure hardship and chapter 4's final charge. Compare the language of God's power with Romans 8:15 and the call to guard teaching with 1 Timothy 6:20.
chapters.lifeApplication: Use your gifts with courage and humility. Do not be ashamed of Christ; hold firmly to the gospel and support faithful servants who suffer for it.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: Courage does not mean reckless exposure to danger or refusal of wise protection. Paul's focus is faithfulness, love, and sound judgement amid real hardship.
chapters.readingNote: Notice Paul's affection for Timothy and the contrast between fear and the Spirit's power, then identify what has been entrusted to guard.
studyQuestions: What does Paul urge Timothy to rekindle?
How does the Spirit answer fear?
What does it mean to guard the good deposit?

chapters.title: 2 Timothy 2 — Endurance, faithful teaching, and handling the word rightly
chapters.historicalContext: Paul uses images of a soldier, athlete, and farmer to encourage steady service. He warns against quarrels and false teaching that can damage the church.
chapters.overview: Timothy is called to endure hardship, entrust teaching to reliable people, and handle the word of truth rightly. The Lord's servant must correct opponents with gentleness and remain useful for good work.
chapters.studyObservation: Faithful ministry requires discipline, transmission of sound teaching, and a character that refuses needless quarrels. Correction aims at repentance and knowledge of truth.
chapters.connectionNotes: Connect the teaching chain with Matthew 28:19–20 and the servant's gentleness with Galatians 6:1. Chapter 3 explains the role of Scripture in equipping God's people.
chapters.lifeApplication: Be steady in service, teach faithfully, and correct others with patience. Invest in trustworthy people who can pass on sound teaching.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: The athletic and military images are metaphors for discipline, not calls to militarise the church or treat people as enemies. Gentleness and patience remain essential.
chapters.readingNote: Follow the three images of service and then note how Paul contrasts quarrelsome conduct with the gentle character of a servant of the Lord.
studyQuestions: What do the soldier, athlete, and farmer teach about endurance?
Why is passing on faithful teaching important?
How should a servant of the Lord correct those who disagree?

chapters.title: 2 Timothy 3 — Difficult times, godly character, and the sufficiency of Scripture
chapters.historicalContext: Paul warns that difficult times will include destructive behaviour and deceptive teaching. He reminds Timothy of the example he has observed and points him to the Scriptures learned from childhood.
chapters.overview: Timothy is urged to continue in what he has learned. Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, correction, and training in righteousness, equipping God's servant for every good work.
chapters.studyObservation: The passage connects the authority of Scripture with its purpose: forming people for faithful life and service. Knowledge that does not shape character falls short of Paul's concern.
chapters.connectionNotes: Read alongside Psalm 19 and 2 Peter 1:19–21, noting each passage's emphasis. Chapter 4 applies this confidence in Scripture to preaching and perseverance.
chapters.lifeApplication: Remain rooted in Scripture and allow it to correct, train, and equip you. Pursue godly character rather than being shaped by destructive patterns around you.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: The list of harmful behaviours should prompt self-examination, not selective condemnation. Scripture's usefulness includes correction of the reader, not only criticism of others.
chapters.readingNote: Notice how Paul's warning about difficult times is answered by Timothy's need to continue in Scripture and follow faithful examples.
studyQuestions: What behaviours characterise the difficult times Paul describes?
Why does Paul tell Timothy to continue in what he has learned?
How does Scripture equip believers for good work?

chapters.title: 2 Timothy 4 — Preach the word, finish the race, and remain faithful
chapters.historicalContext: Paul gives his final charge to Timothy, aware that his own departure is near. He asks Timothy to preach faithfully, remain sober, endure hardship, and complete his ministry.
chapters.overview: Timothy must proclaim the word in season and out of season, correct and encourage with patience, and resist the attraction of teaching that merely pleases hearers. Paul reflects on finishing his race and looks toward the Lord's appearing.
chapters.studyObservation: The urgency of the charge arises from the importance of the gospel and Paul's approaching death. His confidence rests in the Lord who strengthens and preserves him.
chapters.connectionNotes: Connect the charge to preach with 1 Timothy 4:13–16 and the endurance theme with Hebrews 12:1–3. The final greetings show the human relationships surrounding Paul's ministry.
chapters.lifeApplication: Speak truth with patience and courage. Finish the work entrusted to you, support faithful co-workers, and entrust your future to the Lord.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: The charge to reprove and rebuke must not be used to justify harshness or public humiliation. Paul explicitly joins correction with patience and teaching.
chapters.readingNote: Read the final charge alongside Paul's personal reflection, then note how his confidence in the Lord stands beside the reality of abandonment and hardship.
studyQuestions: What does preaching faithfully require in changing circumstances?
What does Paul mean by having finished the race?
How does the Lord's faithfulness sustain Paul near the end of his life?
